RECEIPT CHECK / 001

Record DQ1-01. Round 01. Sheet 001.

A package is counted before it joins the working stock. The outer label is useful for routing, but the contents decide the record. Open one container at a time and keep its loose pieces together until the count is complete.

The tray for item K001 showed a pale diagonal mark. The mark remained visible after a dry wipe. Its position was recorded so that a later check can tell whether it has spread.

If the label and the contents disagree, preserve both readings in the note. A neat total is less useful than a traceable difference. Set the container aside without changing the label, then ask for a second count using the same unit.

COUNT RECORD

Item	Ready	Held	Total
KOO1	25	2.	27
ROO1	29	3	32

The first row records 25 ready pieces and 2 held pieces, giving 27 in all. The second row is a separate group, not an addition to the first. Keep the two item codes distinct when copying these values into a later record.

Closing note: retain record DO1-01 with the tray until the next round. Check the status before moving the contents. A corrected entry must preserve the earlier reading and state why it changed; a blank space must never be treated as a zero.

SHELF ORDER / 002

Record DQ1-02. Round 01. Sheet 002.

A shelf is easiest to use when its order is visible from the aisle. Place the heavier containers on the lower level and keep each item code facing forward. Leave enough room to remove a container without disturbing the next one.

The tray for item K002 showed a pale diagonal mark. The mark remained visible after a dry wipe. Its position was recorded so that a later check can tell whether it has spread.

An empty space is part of the arrangement. Do not fill a gap merely because a small box will fit there. First check whether the gap marks an item awaiting return, a cleaning interval, or a limit on the load of that shelf.

TOOL RETURN / 003

Record DO1-03. Round 01. Sheet 003.

A tool returns to service only after its condition has been checked. Brush away loose material and place the tool on the inspection mat. Compare the working edge with the condition recorded before use, and record any new mark in ordinary words.

The tray for item K003 showed a pale diagonal mark. The mark remained visible after a dry wipe. Its position was recorded so that a later check can tell whether it has spread.

A clean surface does not prove that a tool is ready. Check the joint, handle and retaining pin as separate parts. If a part is missing, mark the whole tool as held; never leave it in the ready tray beside complete tools.

COUNTING METHOD / 004

Record DQ1-04. Round 01. Sheet 004.

A count begins with a defined unit. Loose pieces, paired pieces and sealed packs must not share a column unless the conversion is written down. Read the unit aloud at the start of the count and repeat it when another person takes over.

The tray for item K004 showed a pale diagonal mark. The mark remained visible after a dry wipe. Its position was recorded so that a later check can tell whether it has spread.

Make a short tally after each group rather than carrying a long number in memory. When two counts differ, repeat the smaller group that contains the difference. Do not average the totals: the required result is a count, not an estimate.

COUNT RECORD

Item	Ready	Held	Total
K004	46	5	51
R004	50	6	56

The first row records 46 ready pieces and 5 held pieces, giving 51 in all. The second row is a separate group, not an addition to the first. Keep the two item codes distinct when copying these values into a later record.

Closing note: retain record D01-04 with the tray until the next round. Check the status before moving the contents. A corrected entry must preserve the earlier reading and state why it changed; a blank space must never be treated as a zero.

SURFACE CARE / 005

Record D01-05. Round 01. Sheet 005.

A work surface should be cleared before it is cleaned. Move the loose items into a tray and retain their order. Use a dry cloth first so that coarse particles are removed rather than dragged across the surface during the next pass.

The tray for item K005 showed a pale diagonal mark. The mark remained visible after a dry wipe. Its position was recorded so that a later check can tell whether it has spread.

Inspect the edge as well as the centre. A narrow strip beneath a raised lip can hold material that is missed by a quick wipe. Record persistent marks separately from removable dirt so that tomorrow's check starts from the right condition.

ROO5	5],	2	59

LABEL READING / 006

Record DQ1-06. Round 01. Sheet 006.

Read a label from left to right before copying its code. Similar characters are a reason to slow down, especially where a faint stroke might be part of a letter. Compare the code with the item record only after making an initial reading.

The tray for item K006 showed a pale diagonal mark. The mark remained visible after a dry wipe. Its position was recorded so that a later check can tell whether it has spread.

Keep the old label when a replacement is fitted. Write down the reason for replacement and check that the new label identifies the same item. Clear lettering is helpful, but an attractive label attached to the wrong container creates a larger problem.

DRY STORAGE / 007

Record DOQ1-07. Round 01. Sheet 007.

Dry storage depends on routine observation as well as closed lids. Check the seal before moving a container and look for a change in the paper liner. A small curl at an edge may be the first visible sign that conditions have changed.

The tray for item K007 showed a pale diagonal mark. The mark remained visible after a dry wipe. Its position was recorded so that a later check can tell whether it has spread.

Separate observations from explanations. Record a damp patch as a damp patch; do not record a leak unless its path has been found. Move the affected material to the holding shelf and preserve the arrangement that will help the next inspection.

TRANSFER NOTE / 008

Record DQ1-08. Round 01. Sheet 008.

A transfer note follows the material through each change of location. Record the starting shelf, destination code and quantity before the move. Keep the note with the tray until the receiving position has been checked against the written destination.

The tray for item K008 showed a pale diagonal mark. The mark remained visible after a dry wipe. Its position was recorded so that a later check can tell whether it has spread.

Complete a transfer only after the final count. If the move is interrupted, leave a clear status note and keep the unfinished tray separate. The next shift must be able to tell whether a quantity is waiting to move or has already arrived.

MEASURING EDGE / 009

Record DO01-09. Round 01. Sheet 009.

A length reading begins at the marked zero rather than at the end of the rule. Hold the rule flat and keep the item square to the scale. Read from directly above the mark so that the edge does not hide the nearest division.

The tray for item K009 showed a pale diagonal mark. The mark remained visible after a dry wipe. Its position was recorded so that a later check can tell whether it has spread.

pages.raw_text:
HOLDING AREA / 010

Record DO1-10. Round 01. Sheet 010.

The holding area separates unresolved items from ready stock. Each tray needs one clear reason for being held and a next action that can be completed. A short specific note is better than a broad word that leaves the next reader guessing.

The tray for item K010 showed a pale diagonal mark. The mark remained visible after a dry wipe. Its position was recorded so that a later check can tell whether it has spread.

Review the oldest tray first, but do not release it merely because it has waited. Check that the stated reason has been resolved and preserve the evidence of that check. Move the material and its note together when the status changes.

COUNT RECORD

Item	Ready	Held	Total

COUNTING METHOD / 049

Record D04-04. Round 04. Sheet 049.

A count begins with a defined unit. Loose pieces, paired pieces and sealed packs must not share a column unless the conversion is written down. Read the unit aloud at the start of the count and repeat it when another person takes over.

The tray for item K049 showed a faint code on the upper face. The code was read twice under steady light. Both readings were retained because the final character needs another inspection.

Make a short tally after each group rather than carrying a long number in memory. When two counts differ, repeat the smaller group that contains the difference. Do not average the totals: the required result is a count, not an estimate.

SURFACE CARE / 050

Record D0Q4-05. Round 04. Sheet 050.

A work surface should be cleared before it is cleaned. Move the loose items into a tray and retain their order. Use a dry cloth first so that coarse particles are removed rather than dragged across the surface during the next pass.

The tray for item K050 showed a faint code on the upper face. The code was read twice under steady light. Both readings were retained because the final character needs another inspection.

Inspect the edge as well as the centre. A narrow strip beneath a raised lip can hold material that is missed by a quick wipe. Record persistent marks separately from removable dirt so that tomorrow's check starts from the right condition.
